about: Eight laws on children of unequal mothers and on the position of a woman who outlives her husband. If a father has called his slave-woman’s sons “my sons”, they divide his estate equally with the sons of his wife, and the heir, the wife’s son, chooses from the share (§170); if he never did, they do not share, but they and their mother are to be set free; the wife, once widowed, takes her dowry and the marriage-gift her husband wrote out for her, lives on in his house, and her estate goes to her sons alone (§171). If her husband never gave a marriage-gift, her dowry is made good to her and she takes a share like one heir’s, and her sons may not drive her out if the judges find them in the wrong (§172). If she chooses to leave, she leaves the marriage-gift to her sons, takes her father’s-house dowry, and marries the man of her choice (§172A). If she marries again and has children, all her children, from both marriages, divide her dowry; if she has none by the later husband, her dowry goes to the sons of her “ḫāwirum”, probably her first husband (§173–174). Then come free women married to slaves, of the palace or of a commoner: the slave’s owner may not claim her children as slaves (§175), and when the slave dies, what the couple acquired is halved between his owner and the woman, who takes her own dowry out first and takes her half for her sons (§176–176A). The last law protects a widow’s young sons: she may not remarry without the judges, who look into the property of her first husband’s house and have the couple leave a tablet; the household goods may not be sold, and a buyer loses his silver (§177). Harper’s transliteration writes the Sumerian signs for ‘son’, ‘slave-woman’, ‘house’ and ‘silver’ as Akkadian words, and each was checked on the plate; the few doubtful spellings are marked in the notes.

sentences.i: If a man’s wife has borne him sons, and his slave-woman has borne him sons,
sentences.n: A long law with a long “if”, so read it clause by clause; this unit is the first half of the protasis. šumma awīlum opens it as always. ḫīrtašu is “his wife”: ḫīrtum (Harper: “wife”) is the free wife, set here against the slave-woman. mārī ūlissum is “sons she bore him”: mārī is DUMU with the two plural signs (DUMU{meš}, the plural signs silent), and ūlissum is walādum “to bear” + -šum “to him”, the d of ūlid and the š of -šum merging into ss, as at §167; the last sign, ZUM, is one complex sign, its identification UNCERTAIN, as there. u is the conjunction (the sign U3, “and”). amassu is “his slave-woman”: GEME₂ is two signs (SAL and KUR) and ZU writes -ssu (amat + -šu); Harper prints ama-zu. Slave-woman and wife each bear sons, and the rest of the law is about how those sons divide the father’s estate.

sentences.i: and the father, in his lifetime, has said “my sons” to the sons the slave-woman bore him and has counted them with the sons of the wife,
sentences.n: The father has acknowledged the slave-woman’s sons. ina bultišu is “in his lifetime”: bultum is Harper’s BULTU “life-time” (the root is balāṭum “to live”, so modern editions write bulṭu; Harper prints ti). ana mārī ša amtum ūlidušum is “to the sons whom the slave-woman bore him”: ša “which” opens a relative clause whose subject, amtum, comes first, in the nominative, with the verb last in the subjunctive -u before -šum “to him”; Harper’s ul-du-šum is a shortened spelling, so the vowels of ūlidušum are UNCERTAIN, as at §119 and §137–138. mārūa iqtabi is “‘my sons’ he has said”: mārūa is DUMU{meš}, then the signs U and A, “my sons”, and iqtabi is the perfect of qabûm “to say”, as at §159. itti mārī ḫīrtim is “with the sons of the wife”. imtanūšunūti is manûm “to count” (not the manûm “mina”) in the perfect + šunūti “them”: “he has counted them”; read from the spelling im-ta-nu-šu-nu-ti, its vowels UNCERTAIN.

sentences.i: After the father has gone to his fate, the sons of the wife and the sons of the slave-woman shall divide the property of the father’s house equally.
sentences.n: The ruling: acknowledged sons share equally. warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku is “after the father has gone to his fate”: warka “after”, šīmtim “fate”, and ittalku the perfect of alākum “to go” with the subjunctive -u (the same idiom as at §165–167). ina makkūr bīt abim is “from the property of the father’s house”: makkūr is a Sumerogram Harper reads ŠA.GA (two signs, GAR and GA), bīt is É, and a-ba is Harper’s spelling of abim “of the father”, UNCERTAIN, as at §158. The sons of the wife (mārū ḫīrtim) and the sons of the slave-woman (mārū amtim, GEME₂ with no ending written) divide mitḫāriš “equally”, izuzzū “they shall divide” (zâzum, as at §165). DUMU{meš} does not show the case: as the subject of izuzzū the plural is the nominative mārū, where the genitive and accusative are mārī.

sentences.i: the man’s daughter shall take her dowry, and whatever she and her husband have acquired since they were joined
sentences.n: The ruling begins: mārat awīlim šeriqtaša ileqqi “the man’s daughter shall take her dowry”, the dowry she brought in with her. u mimma ša mussa u šī ištu innemdū iršû is “and whatever, of her husband and of her, since they were joined they acquired”: mimma “whatever”, ša mussa u šī “that is her husband’s and hers” (šī “she”, as at §163), the same clause as the previous unit’s ištu innemdū … iršû. The sentence continues in the next unit with what happens to that shared property.

sentences.i: they shall divide it into two parts; the slave’s owner shall take one half, and the man’s daughter shall take the other half for her sons.
sentences.n: The shared property is halved. ana šinīšu izuzzūma is “into its two they shall divide, and”: šinā “two” + -šu “its”, “into two parts”, izuzzūma the present plural of zâzum + -ma. mišlam bēl wardim ileqqi is “half the owner of the slave shall take”: mišlum “half” in the accusative, then ileqqi “he shall take”; mišlam mārat awīlim ana mārīša ileqqi is “half the man’s daughter for her sons shall take”. So the dead slave’s owner (the palace or the commoner) gets half of what the couple acquired, and the woman, for her children, the other half; her dowry was settled in the previous unit.

sentences.i: They shall look after the house and bring up the young children; they shall not sell the household goods.
sentences.n: What the couple must do: bītam inaṣṣarū is “the house they shall guard” (naṣārum, inaṣṣarū the present plural); ṣiḫḫirūtim urabbû is “the small ones they shall raise” (rabûm, D-stem, “to bring up”, as at §137; ṣiḫḫirūtim, spelled ṣi-iḫ-ḫi-ru-tim, is the small children). unīātim is Harper’s UNUTU, “household goods” (u-ni-a-tim, the plural, a different spelling of the unūt of the next unit). ana kaspim ul inaddinū is “for silver they shall not give”, i.e. they shall not sell them; the verb is plural (inaddinū), as the couple are the subject.

sentences.i: The buyer who buys the household goods of the widow’s sons shall forfeit his silver; the property shall return to its owner.
sentences.n: The penalty for buying them. šayyāmānum is “the buyer” (as at §9–10). ša unūt mārī almattim išammu is “who the household goods of the sons of the widow buys”: unūt is the construct of unūtum, išammu the present of šâmum “to buy”, with the subjunctive -u (spelled i-ša-am-mu; not the šâmum “to fix”). ina kaspišu ītelli is “from his silver he shall lose”, the house wording “he forfeits his silver” (§112–126 ītelli). makkūr ana bēlišu itâr is “the property to its owner shall return”: makkūr is again ŠA.GA (Harper prints ŠA.GA. with a period after GA at XXX 59), bēlišu “its owner” (be-li-šu), itâr the present of târum “to return”, as at §131 and §135–136. The buyer loses both goods and silver; the widow’s sons keep their household goods.

glossary.-ma: and (clause-chaining particle); also “it is X that…”
glossary.-ša: her / its (3rd-person feminine suffix) · on nouns, “her”: after a t the š is assimilated and said ss, spelled with the sign ZA: bīssa (bi-za, or É-za) “her house”, mussa (mu-za) “her husband”, warkassa (wa-ar-ka-za) “her case”, bēlissa (be-li-za) “her mistress”; otherwise written plainly: panīša, mutiša, abiša, šeriqtaša, bēltiša · on an infinitive, the object “her”: ṣabātiša “seizing her” · on a verb-like form: ezibša (e-zi-ib-ša, UNCERTAIN in form) · on a plural noun: mārūša (DUMU{meš}-ša) “her sons”
glossary.-ši: her / it (3rd-person feminine singular suffix, on a verb): ukannūšima “they shall convict her”, inaddûši “they shall throw her”, iqallûši “they shall burn her” · iṣṣabassi (iṣ-ṣa-ba-az-zi) “it has seized her” (the t of the perfect + -ši said ss, spelled -zi) · on the present plural: imannûši “they shall count her”, ibaqqarūši “they shall claim against her” · on the Š-stem: ušērribši “he shall bring her in”, ušamṭaši “he has belittled her” · on a verb, the object “him” (UNCERTAIN): inaddûši “they shall throw him” (§155, the man being thrown into the water; the plate shows the sign ši, which elsewhere is “her”) · ilmassi (il-ma-zi) “he has known her”, ilmassima; iḫḫazzi “he shall take her”; išakkanūši “they shall set her (on a stake)”
glossary.-šim: to her, for her (dative suffix -šim, on a verb; the feminine counterpart of -šum): inaddiššim “he shall give her”, utarrūšim “they shall return to her”, inaddinūšimma “they shall give her, and”, ušallamšimma “he shall make (it) whole for her, and”; not the accusative -ši “her” of ukabbilšima and ubbiršima
glossary.-šu: his / him · -šum “to him, for him” (dative): išakkanūšum, innadnušum · after a dental the suffix is assimilated and spelled with z: …ssu (ṣibat-zu, ṣibassu “its interest”, written after a broken sign); with a noun: ṣibtišu “its interest”, qātīšu “his hand”, damqaršu “his merchant”; tu-šu, te-šu in broken forms · with the same assimilation after a t: aššassu (aš-ša-zu) “his wife”, from aššat + -šu, t + š said ss · on a verb, the object “him”, or “to him” in the dative (Harper writes -šu for -šum): imaggarūšu (i-ma-ag-ga-ru-šu) “they shall agree to him”; on a noun after a preposition: elišu “upon him” · on a Š-stem, “him”: ušaḫḫazūšu “they shall have him take”, ušeṣṣûšu “they shall make him go out” · uktarriṣṣu (ug-dar-ri-zu) “he has slandered him” (ṣ + š said ṣṣ, spelled with ZU) · ikassûšuma “they shall bind him, and” · on nouns: emišu “his father-in-law’s”, ibiršu “his friend”, rabītišu “his senior one”, warkassu “his case”, zittišu “his share”, īnšu “his eye”
glossary.-šum: to him, for him (dative suffix -šum, on a verb): ibaššišum “there is to him”, iqbišum “he said to him”, inaddiššum “he shall give him”
glossary.abum: father: ilik abišu “his father’s fief-duty” · abī (a-bi) construct “father of”: abī mārtim “the father of the daughter” · abim written a-ba in bīt abim (Harper’s spelling, UNCERTAIN)
glossary.adi: up to, times: adi 12-šu “twelvefold” · as a conjunction, “as long as”, with the subjunctive: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard” · adu 3-šu, adu 6-šu “three times, six times (as much)” — the multiplier, spelled a-du (Harper’s variant of adi; the plate has the sign DU) · adi šinīšu “up to his second time” = a second time (as adi 10-šu “tenfold”)
glossary.akālum: to eat; infinitive akālum “eating, food”: akālim “of eating”, in ša akālim ibašši “there is food” (literally “something of eating”) · with a possession as object or alone, “to have the use of” (a house, an estate), literally “to eat it”: ikkal (i-ik-ka-al, present) in adi balṭat ikkal “as long as she lives she shall eat (have the use of it)”; the sense “have the use of” is UNCERTAIN
glossary.almattum: widow (Harper almattu); written with the Sumerian signs NU.MU.SU and not spelled out, the ending is read from the context: almattum “a widow” (nominative, as subject of the law), almattim “of the widow” (genitive); in the sense “woman whose husband has died”
glossary.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · illiku “(where) he went” (preterite, subjunctive -u, after a restored ašar), in the agent law · alākišu (a-la-ki-šu) “his going” (infinitive with -šu): ina alākišu “in his going” · Gt present ittallak (it-ta-al-la-ak) “she shall go away” (the Gt gives the sense of going off; the Gtn would be ittanallak) · ittalak “she has gone” (perfect): ana šīmtim ittalak “she has gone to her fate” · ittalku (it-ta-al-ku) with the subjunctive -u: warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku “after the father has gone to his fate”
glossary.amtum: slave-woman (GEME₂) · amassu (GEME₂-zu) “his slave-woman”, amtam (GEME₂-am), amtim (GEME₂-tim) · plural amâti (GEME₂{meš}) “slave-women”; the exact plural signs are UNCERTAIN
glossary.ana: to, for · with an infinitive, “to, for” (ana kirîm zaqāpim “to plant as an orchard”); “as” (ana kirîm), “into” (ana libbi), “at the rate of” (ana itêšu)
glossary.andurārum: freedom, release from debt-service (Harper): andurāršunu (an-du-ra-ar-šu-nu) “their release”
glossary.aplum: heir, son as heir (Harper aplu; spelled ab-lim, the sign read ab or ap): aplim “of an heir”, in kīma aplim ištēn “like one heir” · also written with the signs DUMU.UŠ (Harper TUR.UŠ, ablu), unspelled: aplum “the heir”, the son who inherits; the Sumerian writing can also mean “eldest son”, the choice rests on the clause (UNCERTAIN)
glossary.awīlum: man; the free citizen, the code’s first legal class
glossary.ašrum: place; ana ašrišu “to its (proper) place” · ašar “where”, with a verb in the subjunctive: ašar illiku “where he went”
glossary.aššum: because (of); concerning · because; with a clause, also “so that”, giving purpose or reason (aššum … lā ṣabātiša, UNCERTAIN in grammar)
glossary.aḫāzum: to take, grasp; Š-stem šūḫuzum “to make take hold” · to take (a wife): iḫuz (i-ḫu-uz) preterite, iḫuzma “he took, and”; present iḫḫaz (i-iḫ-ḫa-az) “he shall take”, which also serves as a permission, “he may take”; iḫḫazu (i-iḫ-ḫa-zu, with the subjunctive -u) “(before) he takes”; infinitive aḫāzim (a-ḫa-zi-im), taking its object in the genitive; taḫḫazanni (2nd person, with -anni “me”) · to take (a wife): iḫuz (i-ḫu-uz) “he has taken (a wife)”, iḫuzma, itaḫazma (i-ta-ḫa-az-ma, perfect + -ma) “he has taken, and”; present iḫḫaz “he shall take”, aḫḫaz “I shall take” (a-ḫa-az, the doubling not written), taḫḫaz “you shall take”; iḫzu (iḫ-zu) with the relative -u: ša aššatam lā iḫzu “who has not taken a wife”; iḫḫazzi (i-iḫ-ḫa-az-zi) “he shall take her” (-ši, z and š merged)
glossary.balum: without · (ina) balum bēl eqlim “without (the consent of) the owner of the field”
glossary.balāṭum: to live; D-stem bulluṭum — muballiṭ “who gives life” · stative baltat (ba-al-ṭa-at) “she lives”, in adi baltat “as long as she lives”
glossary.bultum: life, lifetime (Harper bultu): bultišu (bu-ul-ti-šu) “his life, his lifetime”, in ina bultišu “in his lifetime”; the vowel and the sign TI are as Harper prints them, the noun itself is not otherwise met in these parts
glossary.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor” · bēl kirîm “owner of the orchard” · bēl (be-el), the construct “owner of”, also with a suffix on the noun that follows: bēl ḫubullišu “his creditor”, bēl ḫubulliša “her creditor” · bēl (be-el, not the sign EN) “owner of”: bēl aššatim “the owner of the wife”, i.e. the man entitled to her (my reading)
glossary.bītum: house, estate · bīt karānim “wine-house, tavern” (construct form bīt, written É); bītiša “her house” (É-ša) · bīt awīlim “a man’s house”; bīssa (bi-za, É-za) “her house”, written with É or syllabically with BI + ZA; bītišu (É-šu) “his house”; genitive bītim, accusative bītam, written É alone
glossary.bīšum: movable property, goods, possessions: bīšašu “his goods” · short construct form bīš (bi-iš) before a genitive: bīš qātīšu “his own goods”
glossary.ekallum: palace (É.GAL “great house”) — the crown as owner
glossary.elûm: to go up; here: to forfeit: ina kaspišu ītelli “he goes up out of his silver” — his money is gone · to come up: īteliānim (perfect, feminine plural, with the ventive -nim) “(the sheep) have come up” · to go up; D-stem ullûm — mulli “who raises high” (litany) · ītelli “he forfeits” (ina mimma ša iddinu ītelli “he forfeits whatever he gave”); ī…, …li in broken forms of the same formula
glossary.emēdum: to lay on, impose; with arnam, arnam emēdum “to lay guilt (on oneself)”, i.e. to be in the wrong (Harper emēdu I,1): immidū (i-im-mi-du) “they have laid (guilt), they are in the wrong” (preterite, 3rd plural; the -u is the plural ending, the doubled m is the assimilated d of the root, spelled out in the sign mi); the whole sense of the clause, “the sons are in the wrong”, rests on this reading and is UNCERTAIN in its grammar
glossary.emēdum-N: N-stem of emēdum, to be joined, be attached (Harper emēdu IV,1): innemdū (in-ne-im-du) “they were joined, they have joined (as a couple)”, preterite 3rd plural; ištu innemdū “since they were joined”, said of a man and wife; the sense “joined” is from the N-stem’s passive use and the context
glossary.epēšum: to do, make: epēšim “doing” · to work (land): ippeš(ma) (present): eqlam šipram ippeš “he shall do the work on the field” · to build (?) (a house): bītam ippēšma(?) “he builds a house, and”, the verb broken; iteppuš (?) in a broken line · ippešū (i-ib-bi-šu) “they shall do (work), they shall work” (present plural) · īpušu (i-pu-šu, preterite with the subjunctive -u) “(which) he built”: to make, build (a house)
glossary.erēbum: to enter: iterub “she has entered” (perfect; Harper I,2) · irrubu (i-ir-ru-bu) “she enters” and īrubu (i-ru-bu) “she entered” — present and preterite with the subjunctive -u, after lāma “before” and ištu “after” · irrub (i-ir-ru-ub) “she shall enter” (present, 3rd feminine); irrubu (i-ir-ru-bu) after inūma “when”; īrubma (i-ru-ub-ma) “she entered, and”, īrubu “(where) she entered”; erēbim (e-ri-bi-im) “of entering”, the infinitive in the genitive, in ana bītim šanîm erēbim “to enter another house”
glossary.ezēbum: to leave; Š-stem šūzubum: ušēzib “he deposited (a document)” · īzib (preterite) “he left (over)” · to leave, divorce: izzibši (i-iz-zi-ib-ši, present, “he shall divorce her”) · ezibša (e-zi-ib-ša) “(I) divorce her”, a quoted word, UNCERTAIN in form (the object “her” on a verb is normally -ši) · īzibšim (i-zi-ib-ši-im, preterite) “he left to her”, said of a deed or gift left to someone
glossary.ezēbum-Š: UNCERTAIN: Š-stem of ezēbum “to leave”: to have left, have deposited (a document): uštēzib (uš-te-zi-ib, perfect, 3rd person); the Š-stem šūzubum elsewhere means “to save, rescue”, so the sense with a tablet (ṭuppam uštēzib) rests on the context · ušezzibūšunūti (u-še-iz-zi-bu-šu-nu-ti) “they shall make them leave (a tablet)” (present, 3rd plural, with -šunūti “them”), in ṭuppam … “they shall have them leave a tablet”; UNCERTAIN as before in its sense
glossary.gadum: together with, along with (preposition; Harper gadu): gadum (ga-du-um) šeriqtim “together with the dowry”; takes the genitive
glossary.ina: in, from · at (ina ebūrim “at harvest”); out of (ina bilat kirîm “out of the orchard’s yield”) · “through, by (means of)”: ina maḫāṣim “through beating”, ina pilšim “by a breach”; “regarding”: ina mimma ša … “regarding whatever …”; ina šanat “in the year”
glossary.itti: with · “from”, after leqûm “to take”: itti šarrāqānišu ileqqi “from his thief he shall take”
glossary.ištu: after, since; from; as a conjunction, “after, once”: ištu … īteliānim “after … have come up”
glossary.ištēn: one: šattam ištiatma “one year only” · ištiššu (iš-ti-iš-šu) “for the first time” (ištēn + -šu)
glossary.išûm: to have: lā īšu “he has not” · īšu “he has”, īšû (the subjunctive form, in a clause that continues): ana turrim lā īšû “has not to repay”
glossary.kaspum: silver — the code’s money, written KÙ.BABBAR “shining precious-metal” · kaspim: mišil mana kaspim “half a mina of silver” · with a spelled vowel after the logogram: KÙ.BABBAR-a-am, -i-im, -u-um: kaspam, kaspim, kaspum (accusative, genitive, nominative); kaspum as the subject; the grain-and-silver pair šeʾam u kaspam “grain and silver” · kasap (KÙ.BABBAR, no ending written) construct “silver of”: kasap tirḫatim “silver of the bride-price”
glossary.kīma: like, as · as, like; with a verb in the subjunctive: kīma ubbalu “as he brings (it)” · according to: kīma ṣimdat šarrim “according to the king’s schedule” · “since, when”, before a stative: kīma mimmûšu lā ḫalqu “since his goods are not lost”
glossary.leqûm: to take: ileqqi “he shall take” · ilqi “he took” (il-qi₂), ilqû (subjunctive, il-qu₂-u₂), ilqēma (il-qi₂-e-ma) “he took, and”, ilteqēma (perfect, il-te-qi₂-ma) “he has taken, and”; ša … ilqû “which he took” · ilqēma (il-qi₂-ma) “he took, and” (preterite ilqe + -ma, here without a spelled e); ilteqe (il-te-qi₂, perfect) “he has taken”; ileqqi (i-li-qi₂, present) “he shall take”; leqîm (li-qi₂-im, infinitive, genitive): ina kaspim leqîm “in the taking of the silver” · ileqqûma (i-li-qu₂-ma) “they shall take, and” (present plural + -ma); ileqqēma “he shall take, and” · ileqqû (i-li-qu₂-u) “they shall take” (present plural, without -ma)
glossary.libbum: heart · ana libbi “into”: ana libbi zittišu “into his share”
glossary.lā: not (in subordinate and nominal contexts) · before a noun in the genitive, “without”: lā kanīkim “without a sealed receipt”; in a šumma-clause, “not”: lā ītamar “he did not see”
glossary.lū: or; either (lū … lū “whether … or”); with verb: “let …”
glossary.makkūrum: property, assets — written with the Sumerogram Harper reads ŠA.GA (modern NÍG.GA)
glossary.manûm-count: to count, reckon (the verb; the noun manûm “mina” is another word): imannû(ma) “they shall count” — 3rd plural, impersonal
glossary.maḫrûm: first, former, previous: maḫrītim in šattim maḫrītim “in the previous year” · maḫru (maḫ-ru) “first, foremost” (an adjective or a stative of maḫārum): ša īnšu maḫru, read “the son he favours” (UNCERTAIN) · maḫrūtum (maḫ-ru-tum, plural in -ūtum) “the former ones”, said of children, in contrast to warkûm “later”
glossary.mitḫāriš: equally, in equal parts, on an equal footing
glossary.mutum: husband (short u; Harper “husband”; mūtum “death” is another word, spelled the same, so the sense rests on context): mutiša “her husband”, mussa “her husband” (written mu-za, -ša after the t), mut “husband of” (construct; mut libbiša “the husband of her heart”) · mutiša panîm / warkîm “her former / later husband”, with mutiša followed by an adjective in the genitive
glossary.muškēnum: commoner, dependent freeman (MAŠ.EN.KAK) — the code’s second rank
glossary.mâtum: to die: imtūt (im-tu-ut, perfect) “he/she has died”, so ina šīmātīša imtūt “she died a natural death”
glossary.mārtum: daughter (written DUMU+ti): mārtišu “his daughter” · mārassu (DUMU.SAL-zu, three signs DUMU + SAL + ZU, ZU for -ssu) “his daughter” · mārtaka (DUMU.SAL-ka) “your daughter”, mārtī (DUMU.SAL-i) “my daughter”, mārtim (DUMU.SAL, no ending written) “of the daughter”: abī mārtim “the father of the daughter”
glossary.mārum: son (DUMU) — here: a minor, not yet able to sell · member of a group: mārū ugārim (DUMU A.GÀR{meš}) “the sons of the irrigated land”, the district’s farmers · mār awīlim “a man’s son” (DUMU); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons” (oblique plural, which may include daughters, so “children”); māršu (DUMU-šu) “his son” · mārūša (DUMU{meš}-ša) “her sons” (nominative plural + suffix); mārīša (DUMU-ša) “her son” (genitive + suffix): ana mārīša “to her son” · mārī (DUMU-i) “my son” (-ī “my”); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “children” in mārī ūlissum “children she bore him”; mārū (DUMU{meš}) “sons” as subject: mārū ana ummātim ul izuzzū “the sons shall not divide by mothers”
glossary.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; the subjunctive -u in a ša- or inūma clause); iddinma “he gave, and”; …in, …din in broken forms; inaddin “he shall give”: ana damqaršu inaddin “he shall give to his merchant” · ittadinma (it-ta-di-in-ma) “he has given, and” (perfect); inaddinu (i-na-ad-di-nu) “(which) he gives” (present, with the subjunctive -u) · ittandin (it-ta-an-di-in, perfect with an extra -n-) “he has handed over”: ana kiššātim ittandin “he handed over into service”; ittadin (it-ta-din) “he has given”, i.e. sold; ana maṣṣarūtim inaddin “he gives for safekeeping”; iddinūšumma “they gave him, and” · inaddin also of a woman, “she shall give” · inaddišši (i-na-ad-di-iš-ši) “he/she shall give her” (the n of the stem swallowed before -ši), of a sale: ana kaspim inaddišši “she may sell her”, ul inaddišši “she shall not sell her” · anaddin “I shall give”, with the n merged into the k of -kum: anaddikkum (a-na-ad-di-ik-kum) “I shall give (her) to you”; iddinu (id-di-nu) “(which) he gave”; iddinušum “he gave him”
glossary.nasāqum: to choose, select: inassaqma (present, with -ma) “he shall choose, and …”
glossary.naṣārum: to guard, keep watch over, protect: inaṣṣarma (present, with -ma) “he shall guard, and …”
glossary.nudunnûm: the marriage-gift, what the husband gives his wife (Harper nudunnū): nudunnam (nu-du-na-am, nu-du-un-na-am, accusative) “the marriage-gift”; the final vowel of the base is UNCERTAIN, the accusative -am is plain; distinct from the šeriqtum, the dowry from the bride’s father
glossary.panûm: former, earlier, previous (adjective, from pānum “front”): panîm (pa-ni-im, genitive masculine) “former”, said of a husband, mutiša panîm “her former husband”; set against warkûm “later”
glossary.parāsum: to decide, cut off: iprus · iparrasūma (i-par-ra-su-ma) “they shall investigate, and” (present plural + -ma; Harper: “to decide, to investigate, to inquire into”)
glossary.pānum: front, face: ina pani “in front of” · panīša ištakan “she has set her face”: the idiom for making up one’s mind, resolving to do something; with ana + infinitive “to …” (panīšu, panīša “his, her face”) · idioms: panam šakānum “to set the face” = to make up one’s mind; panīšu wabālum “to carry his face” = to overlook an offence (UNCERTAIN)
glossary.qabûm: to speak, say: iqbû, iqtabi, iqabbûma
glossary.rabûm-D: D-stem of rabûm: to bring up, raise: urabbāšu “she shall raise him” · urabba (present) “he shall raise (the orchard)” · urabbû (u-ra-ab-bu-u) “they shall bring up” (present plural), with young children as object
glossary.ragāmum: to claim, to call out a claim: irgumu (ir-gu-mu, preterite with the subjunctive -u) “(whatever) he claimed” · iraggum (i-ra-ag-gu-um) “he shall claim” (present with the ventive -m): ul iraggum “he shall not claim” · iraggumū (i-ra-ag-gu-mu) “they shall lay claim” (present plural, no ventive): ana wardūtim ul iraggumū “they shall not lay claim for slavery”
glossary.rašûm: to get, acquire: irtaši “he has acquired”, iraššû “he acquires” · iršû (ir-šu-u) “(whom) he has acquired” (the relative -u): ana mārī ša iršû “for the sons whom he has acquired”
glossary.târum: to return: ul itârma “he shall never again …”
glossary.unūtum: household goods, furnishings, gear (Harper unūtu): unīātim (u-ni-a-tim, plural oblique) “the household goods”; unūt (u-nu-ut) “household goods of” (construct state, before the genitive)
glossary.walādum: to bear, give birth to: ūlidušum (ul-du-šum) “(whom) she bore to him” (preterite ūlid, the long ū of a w-initial verb, with the subjunctive -u and the dative -šum; Harper’s spelling is shortened, so the vowels of the form are UNCERTAIN) · ittalad (it-ta-la-ad, perfect) “she has borne” · ūlid (u-li-id, preterite) “she bore”, ūldu (ul-du, with subjunctive -u) · ūlissum (u-li-zum) “she bore him” (ūlid + -šum, d and š said ss; the last sign is one complex sign, its identification UNCERTAIN) · waldat (wa-al-da-at) “she has borne” (stative): ša mārī waldat “who has borne children”
glossary.wardum: male slave (ARAD) · warad (ARAD, no ending written) “male slave of …”, wardam (ARAD-am)
glossary.wardūtum: slavery, the status of a slave (from wardum “slave” + the abstract ending -ūtum): wardūtim (wa-ar-du-tim, genitive) “of slavery”, in ana wardūtim “for slavery, as slaves”
glossary.warka: afterwards, later · as a conjunction before a clause, “after”: warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku “after the father has gone to his fate”
glossary.warkatum: the circumstances, the facts of the case: warkassu “his case” (warkat + šu, t+š → ss) · UNCERTAIN: warkassa (wa-ar-ka-za) “her case” (what is examined and decided) and “her estate” (what she leaves behind), the second reading resting on the context · the estate, the property left behind: warkat (wa-ar-ka-at, construct) bīt mutiša “the estate of her husband’s house”; warkassa (wa-ar-ka-za) “her estate” in the clause adi balṭat ikkal … warkassa ša mārīšama “her estate is her sons’ alone” (UNCERTAIN where the clause fits both senses)
glossary.warkûm: later, subsequent (adjective, related to warka “afterwards”): warkîm (wa-ar-ki-im, genitive masculine) “later”, of the husband, ana mutiša warkîm “to her later husband”; warkūtum (wa-ar-ku-tum, plural in -ūtum) “the later ones”, said of children; the opposite of maḫrûm “first, former” and of panûm “former”
glossary.wašābum: to sit: ul uššab “he shall not sit” (the stone writes uš-ta-ab — a carver’s slip Harper flags) · to dwell: wāšbum (participle, contracted) “the dweller, the tenant” (a conjectured reading, aš-bu-u[m]); wa… “dwell-” in broken forms · stative wašbat (wa-aš-ba-at) “she dwells, lives”: ša ina gagîm lā wašbat “who does not live in the cloister” · stative wašib (wa-ši-ib-ma, with -ma) “he is staying”: ina ḫarrānim wašib “he is staying on the road” · present uššab “she shall live” (uš-ša-ab) and uššamma (uš-ša-am-ma, the b becoming m before -ma) · infinitive wašābam (wa-ša-ba-am) “to live”, in the accusative after a verb
glossary.waṣûm: to go out; ūṣiamma “he came forward” · wuṣîm (wa-ṣi-im, the infinitive wuṣûm in the genitive after ana) “to go out” · waṣīma (wa-ṣi-ma, with -ma) and waṣiat (wa-ṣi-a-at, stative 3rd feminine) “going out”; the PI sign reads wa or wu, ZI is read ṣi, and the nuance of the form is UNCERTAIN
glossary.waṣûm-Š: Š-stem of waṣûm “to go out”: to send out, bring out; of land, to take on lease: ana irrišūtim ušēṣi “he took (a field) for cultivation” · ušeṣṣûšu (u-še-iz-zu-u-šu) “they shall make him go out” (present plural + -šu “him”; Harper writes ṣ as z): ālam ušeṣṣûšu “they shall drive him out of the city”
glossary.zaḫāmum-D: UNCERTAIN: D-stem, to scheme, plot against (Harper “to scheme”; the root is not met elsewhere in these parts, so the sense rests on Harper and on the context): uzaḫḫamūši (u-za-aḫ-ḫa-mu-ši) “they scheme against her” (present, 3rd plural, with -ši “her”; the doubled ḫḫ is the D-stem)
glossary.zinništum: woman (written with the single sign SAL, ŠAL in Harper): zinništam, zinništim, zinništum
glossary.zittum: share, portion (written ḪA.LA): zittašu, zittišu “his share” · zittam (ṣi-it-tam, the ZI sign read ṣi by Harper and zi here, as in ezēbim) “a share”: zittam kīma aplim ištēn “a share like one heir’s”
glossary.zâzum: to divide, share: izuzzū “they shall divide”
glossary.šakānum: to set, place: išakkanūšumma “they shall set for him (a term), and” · išakkanūšum (present, plural, dative -šum) “they shall place (it) for him”, i.e. count it to him · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be put”: ul iššakkan “it shall not be put (in the account)” · to set, put, impose: ištakan (iš-ta-ka-an, perfect, “has set”), išakkan (present) — išakkanšima (i-ša-ak-ka-an-ši-ma, with -ši and -ma) “he/she shall set (it) on her, and”, as in abbuttam išakkan · išakkanūši “they shall set (her on a stake)”, išakkanūšumma “they shall set (it) aside for him, and” · idiom panam šakānum (panam ištakan) “to set the face” = to make up one’s mind · iššakkan also written iš-ta-ak-ka-an (Harper’s reading, UNCERTAIN): andurār amtim iššakkan “the release of the slave-woman shall be established”
glossary.šalāmum-D: D-stem of šalāmum “to be whole, sound”: to make good, restore (Harper: “to restore”): ušallamma (u-ša-lam-ma) “he shall make good, and”
glossary.šanûm: another, a second one: ana šanîm “to another”, šanûm “another man” · feminine šanītum “another (woman)”: šanītam, šanītim (ša-ni-tam, ša-ni-tim), in the accusative and genitive
glossary.šaṭārum: to write; to assign in writing, deed over (Harper: išaddar): ul išaddar “he shall not deed” · išṭuršum (iš-tur-šum) “he wrote for him”: kunukkam išṭuršum “he wrote him a sealed document”
glossary.šeriqtum: dowry, what the bride brings from her father’s house (§138 ša ištu bīt abiša ublam “which she brought from her father’s house”): šeriqtam “the dowry”, šeriqtaša “her dowry”. Harper reads it with q (še-ri-iq-ta-ša, the sign IG read iq) and later editions with k; UNCERTAIN in the form, the meaning rests on §138 · šeriqtiša (še-ri-iq-ti-ša) “her dowry”, šeriqti (še-ri-iq-ti, construct) “the dowry of”: šeriqtaša ša mārīšama “her dowry is her children’s alone”; šeriqtaša ša bīt abiša-ma “her dowry is her father’s house’s alone”
glossary.šinā: two (šinā); šinīšu (ši-ni-šu) “his second (time)”: adi šinīšu “up to his second time”, i.e. a second time
glossary.šumma: if — the word that opens every law of the code
glossary.šunūti: them (masculine plural, accusative): ṣarrūtim šunūti “those criminals” · as the verbal suffix -šunūti “them”: iqallûšunūti “they shall burn them”
glossary.šuāti: that, the aforesaid · as the independent pronoun “him”: šuāti u bīšašu “him and his goods”
glossary.šâmum: to buy: ištām “he bought”, išammu “he buys”
glossary.šī: she, that (feminine pronoun, as the independent word): ŠAL.GEŠ.TIN.NA šī “that tavern-keeper”; the masculine is šū
glossary.šīmtum: fate; one’s natural death: ana šīmtim ittalak “he went to (his) fate” = he died · plural šīmātum “fates”: šīmātīša (ši-ma-ti-ša) “her fates”; ina šīmātīša imtūt “she died in her fates” = she died a natural death
glossary.ḫāwirum: UNCERTAIN: husband (Harper ḫāwirum, from a root also read ḫāʾirum): ḫāwiriša “her husband”, at §135 the husband she had before (so Ungnad’s 1909 glossary: the first husband a girl marries); a rarer word than mutum
glossary.ḫīrtum: wife (Harper ḫīrtu): ḫīrtašu “his wife” · the free wife as against the slave-woman (amtum): ḫīrtim (ḫi-ir-tim, genitive) in mārī ḫīrtim “the sons of the wife”, ḫīrtum (ḫi-ir-tum, nominative) “the wife” as subject
glossary.ṣeḫrum: young; the child: mār awīlim ṣeḫram “the young son of a free man” · plural ṣiḫḫirū (ṣi-iḫ-ḫi-ru) “(who are) small”, said of children, and ṣiḫḫirūtim (ṣi-iḫ-ḫi-ru-tim) “the small ones”; UNCERTAIN whether the first is a stative or the plural of the adjective
glossary.ṭuppum: the clay tablet; the deed: ṭuppašu iḫḫeppi “his tablet shall be smashed” — the sale annulled physically
